assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into controllable, strongly coupled artificial atoms in a cavity, with dispersive readout and coherent control. It is the architectural basis of superconducting quantum processors and a clear step beyond the macroscopic quantum tunnelling work that was recently recognised. Original, conceptually clean and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal with Girvin and Huang; Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered the 2004 strong-coupling experiments. Theory-plus-two-experiment is a natural configuration. Steven Girvin and others are not in the credited names, so the allocation is not complete and some credit is left unresolved.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of independent confirmation across many groups, and the formalism is now standard in quantum technology. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Credit for the original proposal is shared with people outside the supplied names.
Overlap with the broader superconducting-qubit prize already given needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson by two independent experiments completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and is among the most important experimental results in particle physics. The theory was recognised in 2013, so the experimental confirmation is the remaining half.
assessment.attribution: The experiments are collaborations of thousands. Of the supplied names, Jenni and Della Negra and Virdee conceived and led ATLAS and CMS from the proposal stage; Gianotti led ATLAS at the discovery and is a plausible alternative. The choice among the four is genuinely contested and any choice omits many contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature: couplings and spin-parity have been measured in great detail and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The rules and tradition for honouring large collaborations make the laureate selection hard.
Choosing founders rather than discovery-era leaders is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant founded a new classification of band insulators, and the HgTe experiment confirmed it. It opened topological quantum matter as a field with deep theoretical structure and broad experimental consequences.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical contribution; Molenkamp led the HgTe quantum well experiment with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, and Hasan did the first 3D materials observation. Names outside the credited list (Zhang, Bernevig) complicate a fair division.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation over fifteen years, many material platforms, stable interpretation. Haldane's earlier recognition covers the related topological background.
uncertainties: Whether to include Hasan for the 3D topological insulator experiments instead of Mele or Molenkamp.
Topological insulator and quantum spin Hall candidates overlap and the priority question is not simple.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first high-precision full-sky CMB maps and fixed the cosmological parameters to percent accuracy, establishing the standard Lambda-CDM model. This is a lasting, quantitative transformation of cosmology, though COBE and the Planck mission also contribute to the same story.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was PI, Page led key instrument and analysis aspects, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The team and instrument contributions of Wilkinson and others are not in the supplied names, and the credit is a collaborative one.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and extended by Planck and ground-based experiments; very mature. COBE recognition in 2006 and the 2019 cosmology prize reduce the novelty but not the importance.
uncertainties: Possible reluctance to recognise the CMB field again.
Missing names, including the late David Wilkinson, complicate fair attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock idea and its realisation with magic wavelengths gave frequency standards at the 10^-18 level, which is a revolution in precision measurement with applications to fundamental-constant tests and geodesy. Original, clear and technically spectacular.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance frontier, an economical two-person configuration. Credit to contributors such as Hall and Hansch has been acknowledged through the 2005 prize, and other lattice-clock groups are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories; the redefinition of the second is in preparation. Timely.
uncertainties: Whether ion-clock groups also deserve recognition and whether the work will be seen as a continuation of the 2012 and 2005 prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a very active platform for strongly correlated physics with tunable control.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experiments. The first author, Yuan Cao, is not in the credited names, which raises an attribution concern for the experimental part.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced across groups, but the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated and the field is young, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled.
The experimental credit may need to include people outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising the Hubbard model with cold atoms in optical lattices, including the Mott transition and single-site resolved microscopy, created a controllable quantum simulator for many-body physics. Conceptually appealing and relevant to complex many-body systems.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical proposal belongs to Jaksch, Zoller and Cirac, with Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger as the leading experimental developers. Choosing three of five credited names leaves out some decisive contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many groups with a mature technique, but the physics payoffs for open questions (such as the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram) are still unfolding.
uncertainties: Overlap with the cold-atom prize in 2001 and the theory credit allocation make this hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming phase diagram unified glasses, granular matter and foams through a critical point at random close packing and a rigidity transition with nontrivial critical scaling. It is a clear conceptual advance in the statistical physics of disordered matter, though the existence of a true universality class is still being tested.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming picture in 1998; the numerical and theoretical groundwork of O'Hern, Silbert, Witten and others is important and not covered in the supplied names. A two-person prize is a plausible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely studied and influential; mean-field theory of jamming in infinite dimensions by Parisi and collaborators (recognised in 2021 in broader context) gives partial confirmation, but the finite-dimensional picture is unsettled.
uncertainties: Finite-dimensional criticality and the relation to the glass transition are unsettled.
Lasting impact outside soft matter is still moderate.
